import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 14

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/14](https://www.erdosproblems.com/14)
-/

namespace Erdos14

open Asymptotics Filter


/--
The number of integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are not representable in exactly one way
as the sum of two elements from $A$ (either because they are not representable at all, or
because they are representable in more than one way).
-/
noncomputable def nonUniqueSumCount (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((Set.Icc 1 N) \ (allUniqueSums A)).ncard

noncomputable def almostSquareRoot (ε : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  N ^ (1/2 - ε)

noncomputable def squareRoot (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt N

/--
Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_14.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A, ∀ ε > 0, nonUniqueSumCount A ≫ almostSquareRoot ε := by sorry

/--
Is it possible that $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| = o(N^\frac{1}{2})$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_14.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (A : Set ℕ), IsLittleO atTop (nonUniqueSumCount A) squareRoot := by
  sorry

end Erdos14

reformulations.difference: The source writes a lower bound with an implied constant depending only on ε, whereas placing IsBigO under ∀ A syntactically permits its constant to depend on A as well. These formulations are equivalent here because the bound is required for every positive ε.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write E_A(N) = nonUniqueSumCount A N. Apply the Lean bound at ε/2 to obtain E_A(N) ≥ c_{A,ε/2} N^(1/2−ε/2) eventually, with c_{A,ε/2}>0. Since c_{A,ε/2} N^(ε/2) eventually exceeds 1, this implies E_A(N) ≥ N^(1/2−ε). Thus the multiplicative constant can be chosen as 1, independent of A and ε; the sufficiently-large-N cutoff may still depend on the fixed A. Conversely, a bound with a uniform positive constant immediately gives the Lean IsBigO statement. The exact equivalence with ∀ ε>0, ∃ c>0, ∀ A, ∃ N₀, ∀ N≥N₀, c N^(1/2−ε) ≤ E_A(N) is proved as part_i_uniform_constant_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked all three definitions and both theorem statements. The source still marks the problem OPEN, agreeing with both category tags. Direct requests received Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive user agents; the source HTML, its mathematical formulas, and its LaTeX page were recovered through r.jina.ai. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings. It proves that the counted set is always finite, verifies unordered representations with repetition allowed, connects the definition to a computable Finset model, tests six small sets for N=0,…,8, and expands both asymptotic statements. It also checks the zero-input power/square-root conventions and proves the little-o quotient-limit equivalence. The key equivalence proofs were audited with #print axioms and do not depend on sorryAx. The reviewed file is unchanged.
